title: Landfall and Wreck
premise: Hazel Sandoval, a desert ranger still paying off his dead brother's debts, is sent upriver to find a missing survey expedition — and discovers its sole survivor, cartographer Wren Okafor, hiding in a flooded mission with the expedition's stolen compass. The compass points not north but toward the river's forbidden source, where the surveyors found something worth killing for: a spring that could end the region's drought, and a mining consortium willing to bury the truth along with the witnesses. Pursued by the consortium's enforcer, a man Hazel once called friend, Hazel and Wren fight upstream through rapids, canyons, and betrayal, learning that survival has cost each of them more than they can name. At the source, Hazel must choose between duty to the law that made him and love for the ragtag crew who became his family — and he chooses them, flooding the mine, exposing the consortium, and walking out of the canyon alive but changed, carrying a new debt: to stay.
about_author: Sebastian Amberdale is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who spent six seasons on remote waterways before trading a raft for a writing desk. He lives somewhere dry, keeps too many maps, and insists every story should feel like weather coming in.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Compass
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Tracking a petty thief across the flats, Hazel reflects on the debt he inherited from his brother and the badge that keeps him honest and broke. He catches the thief, but the radio crackles: an expedition upriver has gone silent. Emotional beat: restless duty, the sense that his life is a holding pattern.

chapters.title: Orders Upstream
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. His superintendent orders him to investigate the lost survey team — alone, underfunded, unofficial. He buys supplies he can't afford and takes the thief's confiscated river skiff as transport. Emotional beat: resentment hardening into resolve; the first step of a journey he didn't choose.

chapters.title: Water Where Nothing Grows
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Days upriver through narrowing canyons; signs of the expedition appear — a torn tent, a burned supply cache, boot prints heading away from the water instead of toward it. Someone survived and ran inland. Emotional beat: dread mounting; the river feels watched.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Mission
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first appearance). In a flooded ruin, Wren Okafor, the expedition's cartographer, waits with a rifle and a stolen brass compass that doesn't point north. She nearly shoots Hazel before recognizing his ranger's insignia. Emotional beat: terror and exhaustion giving way to wary relief.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren tells her story: the team traced anomalous water readings to a hidden gorge at the river's source — then armed men arrived, took samples, and executed the crew. She fled with the compass, which her late partner modified to find the source again. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; survivor's burden shared across a campfire.

chapters.title: A Voice on the Radio
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A transmission from 'Ranger Vasquez' — Hazel's old friend and mentor — claims rescue is two days downstream. But the details are wrong; Vasquez died years ago. The voice belongs to someone using his call sign. Emotional beat: betrayal foreshadowed; Hazel realizes the hunt has already begun.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Fleeing downstream ambushes, Hazel and Wren gather unlikely allies: Marisol, a smuggler with a fast boat and a grudge; Teo, a teenage stowaway from the mission village; Old Bram, a disgraced geologist who once worked for the consortium. Emotional beat: reluctant company becoming something like a crew.

chapters.title: The Rapids at Serpent's Neck
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A white-knuckle run through lethal rapids while the consortium's gunboat closes behind them. They lose half their supplies but shake pursuit — barely. Teo proves unexpectedly useful. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first flicker of trust between strangers.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Around the fire, Bram admits he mapped the aquifer years ago and was paid to falsify the reports; the drought above is partly the consortium's doing, engineered to force land sales. Emotional beat: shame and the price of complicity; the theme of survival's cost made explicit.

chapters.title: The Enforcer
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Dane Rook). Rook, the consortium's fixer wearing Vasquez's old call sign, reports to his employers and reveals a personal stake: he blames Hazel for a raid gone wrong that ended his career. He offers a bounty to river people for the fugitives' heads. Emotional beat: cold menace; the hunter given a human face.

chapters.title: Village of Ash
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach a river village burned after refusing to inform on travelers. Teo finds family among the survivors; Hazel treats wounds and sees what the debt economy of fear looks like from below. Emotional beat: anger crystallizing into purpose — this is no longer about duty or survival.

chapters.title: Love Against the Logbook
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren alternating POV. A quiet night at anchor; Hazel admits he could end this by arresting Wren for theft and reporting the truth selectively. Instead he tears up his incident log. First kiss. Emotional beat: tenderness and risk; choosing each other over the rules.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Rook's men catch up via a tip from within the crew — suspicion falls on everyone until Bram's old consortium credentials are discovered missing from his pack. Paranoia fractures the group; Marisol threatens to leave. Emotional beat: trust tested to breaking; the found family nearly shatters.

chapters.title: Gorge of the Silent Spring
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The compass leads them into a hidden gorge where the river simply vanishes underground — the source is beneath, in caverns the consortium has already walled and claimed. Evidence of the murdered survey team is staged as an accident. Emotional beat: awe curdling to horror at how thoroughly the truth has been buried.

chapters.title: Into the Under-River
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel, Wren, and Bram descend through the consortium's flooded workings to document the spring and the crime scene. Bram recognizes the engineering: they plan to cap the spring entirely once the land titles clear. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension; proof within reach.

chapters.title: Betrayal Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The traitor is revealed — not Bram, but the rescued thief from chapter one, planted on Hazel's trail all along. He seals the cavern exit and signals Rook. Teo, thought useless, reroutes water pressure to blow a secondary passage. Emotional beat: the smallest member saving everyone; loyalty repaid.

chapters.title: Rook's Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cornered at the surface, Hazel faces Rook alone. Rook offers Hazel his brother's debt erased, his badge restored, everything back — if he surrenders Wren and the evidence. Hazel remembers who he was before the debt owned him. Emotional beat: the book's moral crux; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Hazel refuses; the crew executes a desperate plan — Marisol rams the gunboat, Teo and Bram breach the cap, and the buried spring erupts, flooding the mine and washing the consortium's claim into legend. Rook, refusing rescue, goes down with his employer's ambitions. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; the river taking back what was stolen.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The spring runs free; downstream villages will drink this season. Wren maps the new course of the river — her first honest chart. She and Hazel stand at the water's edge, uncertain what comes next now there's no mission left. Emotional beat: exhausted peace; the beginning of something chosen rather than owed.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Back in town, Hazel testifies before a tribunal, burning his career to do it: naming the consortium, admitting his own compromises, refusing to soften Bram's guilt or his own. The debt collectors come for him anyway — and the crew pays it together, without discussion. Emotional beat: accountability and grace; debts transformed into bonds.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Epilogue-like: Marisol refits the skiff for trade runs, Bram teaches in the mission school, Teo apprentices as a ranger under Hazel's rival-turned-ally. Hazel and Wren keep the broken compass mounted on their wall, pointing nowhere, needing to. Emotional beat: warmth; found family settled into daily life.

chapters.title: Upstream, Always
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A final short chapter: a new distress call on the radio, another silence upriver. Hazel looks at Wren, at the crew already loading the boat, and smiles. Some debts you pay forever, gladly. Emotional beat: open-ended hope; the adventure continues because the family does.
